summary: This note, drawn from a Wikipedia article on the band Queen, covers several topics: cover versions of Queen songs in films, the band's early history and management deal with Trident Studios, its rise to international success in the 1970s, its later performances with Paul Rodgers and Adam Lambert, and the planned biopic about Freddie Mercury. It also describes the album Jazz and Queen + Paul Rodgers' 2005-2006 world tour.
one_line: Wikipedia article excerpt on the rock band Queen, covering its formation, chart success, Live Aid, later tours, films and Freddie Mercury biopic.
key_facts: Anne Hathaway performed a version of "Somebody to Love" in the 2004 film Ella Enchanted.
In 2001, Jim Broadbent and Nicole Kidman performed "The Show Must Go On" in the film musical Moulin Rouge!.
In 1972, Norman Sheffield offered Queen a management deal under Neptune Productions, a subsidiary of Trident Studios.
Freddie Mercury joined Queen in 1970, suggested the name "Queen", and adopted his familiar stage name.
Queen first charted in the UK with their second album, Queen II, in 1974.
"Bohemian Rhapsody" stayed at number one in the UK for nine weeks and popularised the music video.
News of the World (1977) contained "We Will Rock You" and "We Are the Champions", which became anthems at sporting events.
A 2005 industry poll ranked Queen's performance at Live Aid in 1985 as the best in rock history.
Freddie Mercury died in 1991 of bronchopneumonia, a complication of AIDS.
In July 2013, Sacha Baron Cohen dropped out of the Mercury biopic role due to "creative differences" with the surviving band members.
In December 2013, Ben Whishaw was chosen to replace Cohen as Mercury; Peter Morgan wrote the film.
Jazz (1978) reached number two in the UK and number six on the Billboard 200 in the US.
Queen rented Wimbledon Stadium for a day to shoot the video for "Fat Bottomed Girls" and "Bicycle Race", with 65 naked female models.
Queen + Paul Rodgers' 2005-2006 world tour was the first time Queen toured since 1986.
Queen received the inaugural VH1 Rock Honors at the Mandalay Bay Events Center in Las Vegas on 25 May 2006.
